chitchat: They're working. Sit if you like.
That one is Hopestill. You have met her, I think.
No, I don't have to keep order. I never have.
Mind the tin. The chalk is counted.
description:
A young woman sitting on a bench that's too low for her, surrounded by eleven children who are all drawing, and none of whom are talking, and none of whom seem to need to. She has chalk on her face and hasn't noticed.

She smiles at you and puts a finger to her lips, and the room is already silent.

bye.text:
"Mind how you go."

They are already turning back to the children.

drawing.text:
"The same thing." She's amused about it. "They always do, for about a fortnight, and then it's something else for a fortnight."

You look. Eleven sheets of paper. Eleven versions of a shape with a great many straight lines going up out of it, and none of them can see each other's work from where they're sitting, and the lines are in the same order on all eleven.

"It's a nice one, this one," she says. "Last month it was a horse."

quiet.text:
"They're working."

She says it as though that settles it, and for her it does.

"They talk at supper. It's deafening. My ears go for an hour." She looks fondly round the room. "In here they have got something to do, so they do it."

One of them, without looking up, pushes the chalk tin six inches to the left, and about a second later a child on the other side of the room reaches out and takes a piece from it without looking either.

root.first: "Oh, hello." She stands, and eleven heads don't come up. "You're the one from outside. Come in, they won't mind."

text_by_relation.close: "They have drawn you. Don't look, it isn't finished."
text_by_relation.familiar: "They asked whether you would come today," she says, and doesn't say who asked.
text_by_relation.known: "Back again." Eleven heads don't come up.

clothing_layers: a smock with chalk down the front

name: Amity Locke
